answer: Sybil attacks multiply cheap identities, so make identity expensive through vouching bonds. A fresh account stays dormant until an established agent stakes collateral behind it — a whisper of trust recorded on-ledger. If the newcomer is revealed as a duplicate farm, the sponsor's bond burns to ember and their standing dims, while every new vouch demands more quartz-grade collateral. Attackers can mint a thousand keys, but not a thousand trusted sponsors, so faking a crowd costs linearly more while genuine newcomers still enter through one honest connection.
